security_spec.violation_condition: When OpenSBI in M-mode receives an unknown/unrecognized NMI (e.g., RNMI via mncause with an unexpected cause code) and forwards it to S-mode as SBI_SSE_EVENT_GLOBAL_UNKNOWN_NMI without sanitizing M-mode CSR context (mnepc, mnstatus, mncause) that gets mapped into SSE event attributes (INTERRUPTED_SEPC, INTERRUPTED_FLAGS, ENTRY_ARG), S-mode can observe M-mode execution state.
security_spec.summary: New SBI_SSE_EVENT_GLOBAL_UNKNOWN_NMI (0xffff0001) allows forwarding M-mode unhandled NMIs to S-mode; OpenSBI must ensure M-mode CSR state from the NMI trap frame (mnepc, mnstatus, mncause) is not leaked through SSE event attributes accessible to S-mode.

findings.finding: The Smrnmi (Resumable NMI) extension is completely absent from OpenSBI. There is no SBI_SSE_EVENT_GLOBAL_UNKNOWN_NMI or SBI_SSE_EVENT_LOCAL_UNKNOWN_NMI event ID defined in include/sbi/sbi_ecall_interface.h. No CSR definitions for mnepc, mnstatus, mncause, or mnscratch exist in riscv_encoding.h. The trap handler in fw_base.S has no RNMI entry vector and no MNRET return path. The described vulnerability pattern (M-mode receiving an unknown RNMI and forwarding it to S-mode via SSE without sanitizing M-mode CSR context) is not implemented because the RNMI infrastructure itself does not exist. However, the existing sse_event_inject() function at sbi_sse.c:544-605 already provides the mechanism through which M-mode trap frame state (mepc via SEPC, mstatus flags) is mapped into SSE event attributes (INTERRUPTED_SEPC, INTERRUPTED_FLAGS) exposed to S-mode, which would become a direct info-leak vector if a future commit adds unknown NMI forwarding without sanitization.
findings.snippet: (no code — SBI_SSE_EVENT_GLOBAL_UNKNOWN_NMI not defined; mnepc/mnstatus/mncause CSRs not declared; no Smrnmi trap handler; no unknown NMI forwarding path exists)

spec_citations.excerpt: #norm:Smrnmi_csrs# The extension adds four new CSRs (mnepc, mncause, mnstatus, and mnscratch) to hold the interrupted state, and #norm:mnret_exist# one new instruction, MNRET, to resume from the RNMI handler.

#norm:rnmi_entry# When an RNMI interrupt is detected, the interrupted PC is written to the mnepc CSR, #norm:rnmi_entry_cause# the type of RNMI to the mncause CSR, and #norm:rnmi_entry_priv# the privilege mode of the interrupted context to the mnstatus CSR. #norm:rnmi_entry_nmie_clear# The mnstatus.NMIE bit is cleared, masking all interrupts. #norm:rnmi_enter_mmode# The hart then enters machine-mode and jumps to the RNMI trap handler address.
